paragraphs.text: If only every message were as perfect as its messenger.
Knights fight for honor and mercenaries fight for gold. The militia fights for hearth and home.
"A battle's outcome is never certain." —The Southern Paladin
"Nothing can stop the power of life—not even death." —Onean cleric
". . . Our castle's strength Will laugh a siege to scorn." —William Shakespeare, *Macbeth*
Most eagles hunt small animals. The cloudchasers hunt magic.
Twang. You're dead.
"Training? Seeing my crops burnt to cinders was all the 'training' I needed."
They fletch their arrows with the feathers of angels.
A picture is worth a thousand swords.
"North and South meet and angels sing. Voices resound with a righteous ring." —"The Ballad of the Paladins"
"Soldiers wear down and enemies collapse—but the ballista never tires." —Ballista captain
The strength of one. The courage of ten.
A fool knows no fear. A hero shows no fear.
Honorable in battle, generous in death. —Motto of the Kjeldoran Royal Guard
Knights are quick to pledge their loyalty and even quicker to charge into battle.
Kings don't make knights. Actions do.
Some say they have the blood of hawks running through their veins.
Her heart holds the pain of every soldier she's ever healed.
"How smooth his face, how sure his thoughts. I look forward to breaking his mighty will." —The Eastern Paladin
Without warriors there can be no war.
A valiant knight's life has no meaning without honor.
"We have no need for these trinkets. We need only the strength of our swords and the virtue of our hearts." —The Northern Paladin
Like a meteor, it strikes from above without warning. Unlike a meteor, it then carries you off and eats you.
"Fear this no more!"
"Weapons usually bring death. Today, mine will bring life."
"We spent three weeks trying to knock that wall down. Now it's knocking us down." —Onean sergeant
The land will never betray those who gave their lives for it.
"For he on honey-dew hath fed, And drunk the milk of Paradise." —Samuel Taylor Coleridge, "Kubla Khan"
Why does a Samite heal? You might as well ask why a bird flies.
"The peasants labor for my profit. I approve."
He reads the battlefield like a map, always seeking the shortest route to victory.
An angel's blessing prepares a soldier for war better than a thousand military drills.
Her sword sings more beautifully than any choir.
"With one breath, the newborn angel took to the air . . . and the world sighed." —*The Book of Serra*
"If not for the wizard, we'd all be dead now. 'Course, it was him that started all this in the first place." —Onean veteran
The earliest mystics believed that the falcon slit the sky to let the light break through.
"How can anyone fight so much yet enjoy it so little?" —The Western Paladin
The noble paladins draw strength from the courage of others.
They fight so closely together a mouse couldn't slip past their guard.
"Even in the darkest night Stars and angels still shine bright." —Onean children's rhyme
"The key to winning any fight is simply staying alive." —The Southern Paladin
Sometimes the wings of fallen dragons refuse to give up the sky.
You may break her shield, but you'll never break her spirit.
"I rely not so much on the wisdom of age as on the overconfidence of youth."
"It is the duty of the strong to oppose any who threaten the weak." —The Southern Paladin
Sharper than wind, lighter than air.
"Believe in the ideal, not the idol." —Serra
Where psycho meets cyclone.
"It's a poor sort of memory that only works backwards." —Lewis Carroll, *Through the Looking Glass*
Too many wizards spoil the spell, but too many spells spoil the wizard. —Sign on entry to arcane lab
"Knowledge is a feast for the mind. Savor every swallow."
He can drown you in his eyes.
The sea has many secrets, but some are too big to be kept.
"Returne from whence ye came. . . ." —Edmund Spenser, *The Faerie Queene*
"The surface world contains nothing I cannot take." —The Lord of Atlantis
The coral merfolk delight in wrestling with their foes, skinning them alive on the razor-sharp edges of their reef.
"I've seen my master do this a hundred times. How hard can it be?"
"You've thrown your net at the wrong fish." —The Lord of Atlantis
When nothing but second best will do.
Seek balance in all things—as long as the scales are weighted in your favor. —Vodalian saying
"How many people can you save in that thing?" "All of them," replied the mage with a smile.
Scholars in their ivory towers call them "sharks of the sky." Scholars on the road don't call them at all.
"It was as if we fought a shadow." —Onean soldier
"I don't *think* so."
The only thing that flows faster than water is fear.
Like arguing with ice —Vodalian expression meaning "wasting your time"
The deep sleep of winter is not always restful.
It doesn't like having visitors . . . unless it's having them for lunch.
"We'll be easy targets if we remain on the ground. Let's take the fight to them."
A master of tactics, the Lord of Atlantis makes his people bold in battle merely by arriving to lead them.
Of royal blood among the spirits of the air, the Mahamoti djinn rides on the wings of the winds. As dangerous in the gambling hall as he is in battle, he is a master of trickery and misdirection.
The mana that binds the world together can also tear it apart.
"Remove their power, and their will to fight will follow." —Tolarian wizard
Neither head holds a brain—that's located somewhere in the chest—but four eyes aim much better than two.
"Eri phar phesta . . . um, phistor . . . er, phistara . . ."
When you sink a lot of ships, it's easy to find sunken treasure.

"The paladins would be wise not to forget about the Pearl Trident. The merfolk warriors have turned the tide of more than one human war . . . and I have no doubt they shall do so again." —Onean scholar
Little things like morals shouldn't hinder one's ambition. —Pirate creed
Exhausting a wizard can be exhausting work.
It can pass through solid matter—but that doesn't mean it's harmless.
He wastes his amazing talents on proving how amazing he really is.
"Abandon ship!"
"Most people believe magic is only a trick. Why change their minds?"
Storm crow descending, winter unending. Storm crow departing, summer is starting.
Most spies sneak into enemy camps. These spies sneak into enemy minds.
"Secrets? What secrets?"
"Of course she's at the head of her class. All of her classmates have disappeared." —Tolarian renegade
Other birds collect twigs for their nests. Magpies steal jewels for theirs.
Why not ask the winds? —Tolarian expression meaning "Who knows?"
"Nope, there's nothing here either. You guys go on ahead, I'll catch up in a minute. . . . Whoo hoo!"
It can stay aloft for weeks with little or no sleep.
A bored wizard once created a vizzerdrix out of a bunny and a piranha. He never made *that* mistake again.
"Let the air itself protect you, for it is everywhere." —Master wizard
They wondered at the size of it. It wondered which to eat first.
The sky is her stage.
"But high she shoots through air and light, Above all low delay, Where nothing earthly bounds her flight, Nor shadow dims her way." —Thomas Moore, "Oh that I had Wings"
"I dreamt of it once. Now I fear it dreams of me." —Tolarian scholar
To gaze under its hood is to invite death.
"I think little of the foes I've slain. But I'm haunted by the friends I've sent to die." —The Southern Paladin
The bog's touch means death to all but the darkest of hearts.
Grief is a razor that slices the soul.
No thrull has ever been burdened with a long life.
Think of it as a butcher knife with wings.
The bodies of its victims are the only tracks it leaves.
Beware anything born among the dead. —Tolarian saying
The darkness of his shield reflects the inky blackness of his soul.
"Hence 'banishèd' is banished from the world, / And the world's exile is death." —William Shakespeare, *Romeo and Juliet*
The eclipse made it clear whose side the sky was on.
"We live for a thousand years. The death of even one brings untold sorrow." —Elvish elder
"The dead make good soldiers. They can't disobey orders, they never surrender, and they don't stop fighting when a random body part falls off." —Nevinyrral, *Necromancer's Handbook*
"Change your mind, or I'll change it for you."
"There is no worse enemy. His passion for death doesn't just border on insanity, it wallows in it." —The Southern Paladin
A single germ can kill more soldiers than ten thousand blades.
"Why do you weep for the dead? I rejoice, for they have died for me." —Fallen angel, to Serra
"Booga booga booga!"
The villagers call it "winged stench."
"It's hard to keep our own troops from fleeing when he's like this. How can our foes possibly stand against him?" —Field marshal for the Eastern Paladin
Toren had stepped on a lot of bugs during his life, so he couldn't help feeling embarrassed when a bug stepped on him.
A full coffin is like a full coffer—both are attractive to thieves.
An advisor once asked the Western Paladin how much gold would be enough. "I have no need of fools who can imagine 'enough,'" he told the advisor's corpse.
A hollow dog is never empty. It is filled with thirst for the hunt.
Whether it howls for hunger or for joy, you're in trouble just the same.
"East and West meet and angels cry. Unholy power darkens the sky." —"The Ballad of the Paladins"
"Brackish water, dark and blind Heed my will, to you I bind." —Opening passage of Leshrac's Rite
On darkness feeding, in nightmares breeding.
Memories cut from the mind can cut right back.
What wizards fear most is losing their minds.
No fear. No sense. And soon, no lunch.
The thunder of its hooves beats dreams into despair.
The Eastern Paladin doesn't attack at night for the tactical advantage. He does it for the sheer joy of fighting beneath the moon.
"Defeating an enemy is not nearly as satisfying as watching one suffer." —The Western Paladin
"You won't be needing this."
"I want every last one of these tree-hugging, earth-loving, pointy-eared weaklings out of here. Now!"
No one knows whether they were named for the diseases they carry or for the speed at which they multiply.
He hunts what might have been.
The earth cannot hold that which magic commands.
They'll chew through armor, flesh, and bone. They'll even chew through each other if they're hungry enough.
The battle's end is the meal's beginning.
It eats death and drinks pain.

"They groaned, they stirred, they all uprose, Nor spake, nor moved their eyes; It had been strange, even in a dream, To have seen those dead men rise." —Samuel Taylor Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"
They're the fiercest of all the Western Paladin's soldiers. They're also the most fiercely loyal—but that loyalty comes at a price.
You are who you eat.
What it lacks in backbone, it makes up for in cruelty.
When the strands call, only the dead answer.
The assassin sees only throats and hears only heartbeats.
Pockets of Æther can be so foul they melt flesh from bone.
"I don't *feel* any different."
A skeletal wall, strengthened by the souls of traitors, rings the city of the Eastern Paladin.
"Expect nothing but scorn, flattery, and lies. And never turn your back on him." —The Northern Paladin
The warping of bodies and souls has become the heart of Yawgmoth's existence.
As the foul beast appeared, arcane lightning crackled around it.
"From the snowy slopes of Kaelor, To the canyons of Bandu, We drink and fight and feast and die As we were born to do." —Balduvian tavern song
The generals were dead. The battle plans were forgotten. It was everyone for themselves.
Fire never dies alone.
After their first encounter, the goblins named him Chuck.
"It is a slaughter, the death of a sea. Never speak of it again." —The Lord of Atlantis
The hellkites are artists with flames, painting the world with fire.
"Fire hurts them almost as much as the chaos that follows. Almost." —The Western Paladin
The intensity of their glare was soon surpassed by the intensity of their attack.
A reward is worthless if you aren't around to enjoy it.
It treads on feet of coals and strikes with the force of a volcano.
The Ghitu believe their race was born of fire, and it's an honor to return to it.
The hardest part of his training is learning not to eat the boar.
"Dig. Dig. Dig. Dig. Dig. Dig. Die!" —Goblin chant
We're *elite*. You're not. —Infantry motto
Years of attempts have brought the goblins no closer to growing a sausage tree.
"What's got two arms, one wing, and no brains?" —Ghitu riddle
To be king, Numsgil did in Blog, who did in Unkful, who did in Viddle, who did in Loll, who did in Alrok. . . .
He's smart for a goblin. He can do *two* things: hit *and* run.
Goblins prefer caves to just about anything else. Caves prefer just about anything else to goblins.
The goblin idea of music is to hit something with a stick.
"Let me introduce you to Rocky."
Hill giants are mostly just big. Of course, that does count for a lot.
"I'm going to count to three. Three."
"Some have said there is no subtlety to destruction. You know what? They're dead." —Wandering mage
"Catch!"
"I'll climb down soon. Don't worry, it's just a thundersto—" —Former elvish scout
"A flash of the lightning, a break of the wave, He passes from life to his rest in the grave." —William Knox, "Mortality"
Ogres learn how to smash stuff even before they learn how to walk.
"Ready . . . aim . . . fire!" "Ow!"
"Burn their homes. Salt their lands. Nothing survives." —The Western Paladin
Do not judge a lizard by its size. —Ghitu proverb
"When the air burns, only death breathes deep." —Bogardan mage
"Who says lightning never strikes twice?" —Storm shaman
He raged at the world, at his family, at his life. But mostly he just raged.
Those who play with fire are bound to get burned.
"Be as fast as lightning, and you will be just as deadly." —Combat trainer
"Mercy? Mercy is for the playground, not the battleground."
"Here, kitty kitty. Here, kitty kitty. Aaaaugh!"
Earth arms itself with fire.
The undisputed master of the mountains of Shiv.
"We were ready for an attack from the front, sides, or back—but the mage hit us from below." —Veteran soldier
She speaks with the voice of the winds, and the earth trembles.
Caught red-handed.
"That arm's for bashin'. That one's for smashin'. That one's for scratchin'. And that one . . . I don't know what that one's for." —Orgg trainer
Where do you run when the earth becomes your enemy?
Fire finds its form in the heat of the forge.
The erupting flames work as both barrier and weapon.
Fire is always at the top of the food chain, and it has a *big* appetite.
You'll never find an anaconda in a swamp. It will always find you first.
The Phyrexian killing machines couldn't have known the seriousness of their mistake in wounding the ape—they'd never seen it angry.
"There's never been a dwarven smith who could match the marvels that Gaea herself forges." —The Elvish Champion
The merfolk may rule the waters, but hippos have never had much respect for authority.
It keeps the upper reaches of the forest free of every menace . . . except for the spider itself.
A fruit must rot before its seed can sprout. —Yavimaya saying
Mold crept over the walls and into every crevice until the gleaming white stone strained and burst.
"Give it a week and it will feed an army."
"I may seem wise to you, but I'm merely a sapling among mighty oaks."
The archers have a reputation for attacking without warning. They claim that the first arrow *is* the warning.
"For what are leaves but countless blades To fight a countless foe on high." —Elvish hymn
To an elf, magic and music are the same.
From Gaea grew the world, and the world was silent. From Gaea grew the world's elves, and the world was silent no more. —Elvish teaching
More than any other battlefield, the forest gives the advantage to those who know it best.
"Bet you can't put it through the eye." "Left or right?"
"It is useful to be able to speak to the trees. But it is truly wondrous to be able to listen to them."
"I felt the ground shake, so I hid in my tent until the earthquake passed. It passed all right, and it left hoofprints." —Femeref explorer
Watching the spider's web —Llanowar expression meaning "focusing on the wrong thing"
A gorilla chief must always be prepared to defend his crown. This leads to some pretty tough apes.
They've got claws as long as your arm. And they're grouchy. Really, really grouchy.
Llanowar covers a million square miles, yet nobody enters the forest without the elves knowing it.
A wolf without a pack is either a survivor or a brute.
"When the forest wants something, no mortal mind can resist her." —Maro
No two see the same Maro.
"Guess where I'm gonna plant this!"
Get in touch with your inner monster.
"The dead whisper to the living. If you listen, you will learn." —Maro
The land rises up to defend against those who would spoil its beauty.
There's only one thing worse than a hungry lion—many hungry lions.
Nature grows solutions to her problems.
The wise pay as much attention to what they throw away as to what they keep.
And would you strip the bark from a treefolk? —Elvish expression meaning "Are you crazy?"
"Why should death always have the last word?" —Llanowar druid
Those who understand the forest are free to harvest its bounty.
"One piece? Now there's a hundred!"
Seekers spend their lives protecting a home they rarely visit.
Where dryads dance, seeds sprout and flowers bloom.

"I wouldn't stand in front of that wurm, son. 'Course, I wouldn't stand behind it neither. In fact, standing anywhere near that wurm's not much of a plan. Running, now *that's* a plan!" —Wandering mage
"May the winds blow till they have wakened death. . . ." —William Shakespeare, *Othello*
Rain from this storm leaves you pinned to the ground like an insect.
"Their thoughts flow through my mind, and I am healed." —Fyndhorn elder
Armodons are trained to step on things. Enemy things.
Even the grandest forest begins with a single seedling. —Llanowar saying
No forest is so remote that the elves don't know its secrets.
Each spell has its own song, and the enchantress knows the dance for each.
Spring breathes the magic of new life.
If you stop to listen, you can hear it grow.
The elves long ago mastered the art of hunting with nets. They call it "fishing the sky."
Every branch a crossroads, every vine a swift steed.
Her roots connect her to the forest's wishes.
Some say Aladdin's third wish was for this ring.
The heavier the load, the harder it works.
The Eastern Paladin knew how highly his southern rival valued horses, so he gleefully prepared a suitable welcome.
Polished by a thousand waves.
Legend has it that the world was hatched from a dingus egg.
Bridges usually get you from one place to another. This one just gets you.
Feroz is gone, but what remains is his final gift to his people: the right to be left alone.
"Wheeeeeeeeeeeeeee!"
"Every day, I fight for my life and win. Every night, I fight to remember my name and lose."
The Southern Paladin taught the airborne vermin to fear the storm that rains upward.
Legend has it that the mine howls out the last words of those who died inside.
Forged by a thousand flames.
Blessed by a thousand prayers.
Most books simply deliver knowledge. This one expects some in return.
Your heart's desire is found within. —Saddlebag inscription
"Knowledge is power." —Sir Francis Bacon, *Meditationes Sacrae*
The bigger they are, the stronger its pull.
More than one mage has been driven insane by the sound of the millstone relentlessly grinding away.
Its wings were only designed to be ornamental, but it learned to use them on its own.
It doesn't think. It doesn't feel. It doesn't laugh or cry. All it does from dusk till dawn Is make the soldiers die. —Onean children's rhyme
Never forget your feet —Elvish expression meaning "watch your step"
The rod is a relic from ancient times . . . cruel, vicious, mean-spirited times.
"I'm not one for pretty things," said Sisay. "Unless they're pretty useful as well."
Knowledge knows no bounds.
The warriors fought against the paralyzing waves until even their thoughts froze in place.
Tainted by a thousand fears.
"A stick is your friend. A pointed stick is your good friend. An army of pointed sticks is your best friend." —Onean sergeant
Strengthened by a thousand limbs.
